problem: Which of the following is **NOT** a first-order linear ordinary differential equation?

feedback.problem: Which of the following is **NOT** a first-order linear ordinary differential equation?
feedback.worked_solution:
To determine which of the following differential equations is a first-order linear ordinary differential equation, we attempt to write each option in the standard form.

A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Let's attempt to write $y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+x=y$ in the standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+x=y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+x{y}^{-1}=1\end{aligned}
$$

This differential equation cannot be written in standard form since the power of $y$ in the term $x{y}^{-1}$ is not $1.$ Since the equation cannot be written in standard form, we conclude that it is not a first-order linear ODE.

All of the other equations can be written in the standard form, and therefore they are first-order linear ODEs.
